Practising since 2003, in Northern Virginia since 2013, entirely on prosthodontics. Diplomate of the American Board of Prosthodontics and Fellow of the American College of Prosthodontists.

Adjunct faculty at Virginia Commonwealth University, teaching the residents in its Prosthodontics Postgraduate Program, and lecturing on smile design and implants. Which is what brings the difficult cases to his door.
Adjunct faculty at Virginia Commonwealth University
Across that career, over 18,000 implants placed and over 15,000 arches restored.

FP1, FP2, FP3, and why we plan for the first.

Every full-arch implant prosthesis is one of three types. What separates them is how much of it is teeth, and how much is pink acrylic standing in for gum and bone. Most practices fit one kind. Here the arch is planned as thin as the case will carry.

FP1Replaces teeth onlyNatural crown-and-bridge lookNo added pink, no extra bulkTypically on more natural gum architectureFP2Longer teeth, minimal pinkLonger teeth, minimal pink acrylicThe pink that is added still follows the natural gum contourRarely indicated, and often not idealFP3Replaces teeth,...
